analysis.title: NVIDIA Corp: Media Reports on CEO Change; A Few Thoughts
key_insights: Media reports say NVDA's Board is preparing to oust Jensen Huang as CEO and is working with an outside firm to identify successor candidates. UBS expects the company would find a strong candidate but sees the impact being felt widely.

Financing: NVDA has become a key source of funds for neo-clouds, LLM developers, ecosystem partners and suppliers, and UBS sees Huang as the driving force behind this. Even if a new leader keeps the approach, UBS expects a near-term pause in the company's willingness and ability to pursue such deals.

UBS estimates NVDA generates ~$50-60B per quarter in FCF, a big portion of which has been put back into the AI ecosystem. A pause could take ~$50B or more out of the system, at least temporarily, while interest rates are rising and parts of the credit market have become less liquid.
Supply chain: NVDA has been ahead of peers on long-term supply agreements for memory, substrates and other areas. UBS viewed Huang as singular in procurement and out in front of some key peers.
Regulation: UBS could see the US government enforcing tighter restrictions on NVDA (and AMD) shipments into China, and more importantly into regions such as Singapore or Malaysia.

Singapore was nearly 20% of NVDA revenue when geographic disclosures changed in mid-C2025. Assuming a portion of that plus some of the now-small China revenue is at risk, UBS estimates exposure of roughly 10% of revenue.
UBS says the longer-term product roadmap and other issues also matter, but for any company this goes beyond the CEO and any impact would take years to manifest.
Buy rating and $300 price target unchanged, based on ~14x C2028E P/E applied to C2028E EPS of $22.08. Price was $173.73 on 11 Nov 2026, implying 72.7% forecast price appreciation.

market_movers.rationale: PT unchanged at $300 on ~14x C2028E EPS of $22.08 despite media reports of a CEO change. UBS flags financing, supply chain and export-restriction risks.

earnings_insights: UBS diluted EPS estimates for NVDA: FY 01/27E $9.57 vs consensus $9.30, 01/28E $17.16 vs consensus $15.86, 01/29E $22.08 vs consensus $21.05. These are UBS estimates against consensus, not reported figures.
UBS quarterly EPS estimates: Q3E $2.53 vs consensus $2.48 and Q4E $2.95 vs consensus $2.75. Q1 $1.87 and Q2 $2.22 are shown at the same level for UBS and consensus.
UBS revenue estimates (forecast): FY01/27E $420.3B, FY01/28E $744.2B, FY01/29E $985.1B, against $215.9B reported for FY01/26.
risk_factors: Leadership transition: Huang's possible removal as CEO and the uncertainty around a successor.
Pause in NVDA's AI ecosystem financing, potentially ~$50B or more, while rates are rising and credit liquidity is thinner.
Loss of Huang's procurement leadership on long-term supply agreements.
Tighter US export restrictions affecting China, Singapore and Malaysia, with roughly 10% of revenue at risk in UBS's estimate.
Competition from AMD and Intel and cyclicality in semiconductors, per the report's standard risk statement.
geopolitical: Potential for tighter US export restrictions affecting NVDA and AMD shipments into China, and more so into Singapore and Malaysia.
